archives.source: archive copied directly from existing installer payload

scope: Fresh output directory for every extraction; archive and filesystem cache were warm. These are not cold-start or end-to-end install measurements.

Managed stopwatch includes SevenZip.ExtractAsync and managed decoder first-call/JIT work occurring inside this timed call. It excludes dotnet process startup, installer UI startup, payload archive copy from EXE, installation final copy, shortcuts, registry operations and uninstaller generation.
Native stopwatch includes 7z process launch and complete extraction to fresh output; native command extracts all 437 files in the same level9 archive.
The level9 archive was not recompressed. The level5 and level7 archives contain exactly the extracted source files and were compressed with 7z a -t7z -m0=lzma2 -mx=N using defaults otherwise.
Some exploratory managed runs overlapped unrelated local compression. The final managed level9 run began after all reported other-agent compression finished.
Level5 and level7 are single measurements and should not be used to claim a precise decoding-speed difference. Compression times are exploratory and may overlap other processes.

The prepare run (19.3470433 seconds) produced the reference source directory. The nine additional outputs (five managed and four native) were SHA256 checked against that reference; see hash-checks.json. There were ten timed extraction runs in total.
